name: Cryptography
description: How modern cryptography works: ciphers, hashes and MACs, public-key systems, signatures and the protocols built from them.

nodes.name: Goals & adversaries
nodes.desc: Confidentiality, integrity, authenticity and Kerckhoffs's principle.
nodes.summary: You will be able to state the goals of cryptography, model adversaries and explain Kerckhoffs's principle.

nodes.name: Classical ciphers
nodes.desc: Caesar, Vigenère and substitution ciphers and how to break them.
nodes.summary: You will be able to encrypt with Caesar, Vigenere and substitution ciphers and break them with frequency analysis.

nodes.name: Perfect secrecy
nodes.desc: One-time pad, Shannon's perfect secrecy and why it is impractical.
nodes.summary: You will be able to define Shannon's perfect secrecy, prove the one-time pad achieves it and explain why it is impractical.

nodes.name: Computational security
nodes.desc: Security against efficient adversaries, negligible advantage and pseudorandomness.
nodes.summary: You will be able to define security against efficient adversaries using negligible advantage and pseudorandomness.

nodes.name: Block ciphers & AES
nodes.desc: Block ciphers, substitution-permutation networks and AES.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how block ciphers work and describe the structure of AES as a substitution-permutation network.

nodes.name: Stream ciphers
nodes.desc: Pseudorandom generators, ChaCha20 and the danger of nonce reuse.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe stream ciphers built from pseudorandom generators such as ChaCha20 and explain the danger of nonce reuse.

nodes.name: Modes of operation
nodes.desc: ECB, CBC, CTR and why the mode matters.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compare ECB, CBC and CTR modes and explain why the choice of mode affects security.

nodes.name: Hash functions
nodes.desc: Collision, preimage and second-preimage resistance, SHA-2 and SHA-3.
nodes.summary: You will be able to define collision, preimage and second-preimage resistance and describe SHA-2 and SHA-3.

nodes.name: MACs
nodes.desc: Message authentication codes and HMAC.
nodes.summary: You will be able to authenticate messages with MACs and HMAC and explain why naive hash-based MACs fail.

nodes.name: AEAD
nodes.desc: Encrypt-then-MAC and AEAD modes like AES-GCM.
nodes.summary: You will be able to combine encryption and authentication correctly with encrypt-then-MAC and AEAD modes such as AES-GCM.
topics: Why encryption alone is not enough

nodes.name: Password hashing
nodes.desc: Salts, key stretching, bcrypt, scrypt and Argon2.
nodes.summary: You will be able to store passwords safely using salts, key stretching and algorithms like bcrypt, scrypt and Argon2.

nodes.name: Public-key basics
nodes.desc: Key pairs, trapdoor functions and hard problems behind public-key crypto.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how key pairs, trapdoor functions and hard mathematical problems make public-key cryptography possible.

nodes.name: RSA
nodes.desc: Key generation, encryption, padding and why textbook RSA is insecure.
nodes.summary: You will be able to generate RSA keys, encrypt and decrypt, and explain why textbook RSA needs padding such as OAEP.

nodes.name: Diffie-Hellman
nodes.desc: Key exchange over groups and the discrete logarithm problem.
nodes.summary: You will be able to perform Diffie-Hellman key exchange over a group and relate its security to the discrete logarithm problem.

nodes.name: Elliptic curves
nodes.desc: Elliptic-curve groups, ECDH and why keys are shorter.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe elliptic-curve groups, perform ECDH and explain why elliptic-curve keys are shorter for equal security.

nodes.name: Digital signatures
nodes.desc: RSA and ECDSA/EdDSA signatures and hash-then-sign.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how RSA, ECDSA and EdDSA signatures work and why messages are hashed before signing.

nodes.name: PKI & certificates
nodes.desc: Certificates, certificate authorities, chains of trust and revocation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how certificates, certificate authorities and chains of trust bind keys to identities, and how revocation works.
topics: Chains of trust and root stores

nodes.name: TLS
nodes.desc: The TLS 1.3 handshake, forward secrecy and record protection.
nodes.summary: You will be able to walk through the TLS 1.3 handshake and explain forward secrecy and record protection.

nodes.name: Attacks & misuse
nodes.desc: Padding oracles, timing side channels and common implementation mistakes.
nodes.summary: You will be able to recognise padding oracle attacks, timing side channels and common implementation mistakes in cryptographic code.

nodes.name: Zero-knowledge proofs
nodes.desc: Proving a statement without revealing why, and where ZK proofs are used.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how zero-knowledge proofs prove a statement without revealing the reason, and where they are used.

nodes.name: Toy RSA project
nodes.desc: Implement RSA key generation, encryption and signing from scratch, then attack weak parameters.
nodes.summary: You will implement RSA key generation, encryption and signing from scratch and then attack keys with weak parameters.
topics: Attacking small exponents and close primes

nodes.name: Secure chat project
nodes.desc: Build an end-to-end encrypted chat with key exchange, AEAD and authenticated peers.
nodes.summary: You will build an end-to-end encrypted chat with key exchange, AEAD encryption and authenticated peers.
